s.c: The expression εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες, literally ‘talking into the air,’ may be regarded as a type of idiom meaning ‘talking to no purpose’ or ‘talking without anyone understanding.’ Accordingly, ἔσεσθε γὰρ εἰς ἀέρα λαλοῦντες may be rendered as ‘you will be talking, but no one will understand’ or ‘you will be talking, but your words will not enter anyone.’ In ⟦Acts 22:23|Acts 22:23⟧, κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα ‘throwing dust into the air,’ it may be more appropriate in a number of languages to say ‘throwing dust above themselves’ or simply ‘throwing dust up.’ A literal rendering of ‘throwing dust into the air’ might suggest in some languages that the air was some kind of a container in which the dust remained.|The Greek term ἀήρ in ⟦Revelation 9:2|Revelation 9:2⟧ (ἐσκοτώθη ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ὁ ἀὴρ ἐκ τοῦ καπνοῦ τοῦ φρέατος ‘the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the pit’) may very well be translated as ‘air,’ but since it is a reference primarily to space rather than to substance, it is more natural in a number of languages to say ‘the sky was darkened by the smoke from the pit.’

In some languages it may be quite impossible to translate literally ‘hitting the air,’ for since the air is not regarded as a kind of material substance, it is impossible to hit it. s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Powers
s.d: (title for supernatural forces and powers) a supernatural power having some particular role in controlling the destiny and activities of human beings
s.g: power; authority; lordship; ruler; wicked force
s.c: Some scholars have believed that it is possible to reconstruct at least in part some of the hierarchy represented by these various supernatural forces and powers, on the basis of the neoplatonic system of nine such powers arranged in three orders of three each. NT terminology and usage does not, however, lend itself to such a classification, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to determine what are the significant differences between these supernatural powers and forces.|For the most part, translators have endeavored to render the various terms in somewhat different ways, for example, ἐξουσία as ‘authority’; δύναμις as ‘power’; κυριότης as ‘ruler’; and phrases such as τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις as ‘wicked spiritual forces in the heavenly world.’ In a number of languages, however, there are simply not enough terms to designate various kinds of powers, authorities, and forces which could be employed in speaking of such supernatural impersonal powers. Accordingly, some translators have simply used a phrase such as ‘any and all kinds of supernatural powers.’ Where it is possible to make certain lexical distinctions between terms and phrases, this, of course, should be done, but in a number of contexts this may be impossible, and accordingly, some explanation in a marginal note may be required if the reader is to understand satisfactorily the intent of the passages in question.|In some instances a measure of meaning may be obtained by somewhat paraphrastic expressions. For example, ⟦Ephesians 2:2|Ephesians 2:2⟧ is rendered in some languages as ‘at that time you lived in the way in which the spirit that governs this world dictated you should live. This is the way the one who rules over the power in space commanded you to live. This is the very spirit that now commands the people who disobey God.’

It is simply a colorless fluid which was mixed with blood.|In ⟦Revelation 8:8|Revelation 8:8⟧ (καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῆς θαλάσσης αἷμα ‘and a third of the sea became blood’) and ⟦Revelation 11:6|Revelation 11:6⟧ (καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσιν ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων στρέφειν αὐτὰ εἰς αἷμα ‘and they had power over the waters to turn them into blood’) the reference may not be to blood as a substance but to the blood-like color of the objects in question.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:αἷμα<SDBG:αἷμα:000000>}[a] ‘blood,’ {D:8.64}) the death of a person, generally as the result of violence or execution
s.c: It is possible to interpret αἷμα in ⟦Romans 5:9|Romans 5:9⟧ (δικαιωθέντες νῦν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ ‘by his death we are put right with God’) as primarily a reference to physiological death. But in such contexts in which αἷμα is used in speaking of the death of Christ, there is no doubt an additional component derived from the occurrence of αἷμα in contexts speaking of atoning sacrifice. Therefore, one may analyze the meaning of αἷμα in such contexts as meaning ‘sacrificial death’ and not merely physiological death. In ⟦Romans 5:9|Romans 5:9⟧ and similar contexts, a number of translators have preferred to preserve an often recurring phrase such as ‘the shedding of his blood.’ However, in English this can be somewhat ambiguous in that ‘the shedding of blood’ normally refers to the killing of someone else and not to experiencing death. See also LN 23.112.

s.dp: Time › Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
s.d: a unit of time as a particular stage or period of history
s.c: In a number of languages there is no specific term for ‘age’ or ‘era.’ The closest approximation in the context of ⟦Matthew 12:32|Matthew 12:32⟧ may be ‘not in these many years and not in the many years which will follow.’|In ⟦1 Timothy 1:17|1 Timothy 1:17⟧ (τῷ δὲ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων literally ‘to the king of the ages’) the genitive phrase τῶν αἰώνων is better understood as an abstract of unlimited extent of time, and accordingly, one may translate more accurately as ‘the eternal king.’ Compare LN 67.95.

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Universe, Creation
s.d: the universe, perhaps with some associated meaning of ‘eon’ or ‘age’ in the sense of the transitory nature of the universe (but this is doubtful in the contexts of {S:05800100200038} and {S:05801100300010})
s.c: In ⟦Hebrews 1:2|Hebrews 1:2⟧ it may be essential in a number of languages to translate ‘he is the one through whom God created everything,’ though in some instances a more idiomatic and satisfactory way of rendering the meaning would involve a phrase such as ‘… created both the earth and the sky’ or ‘… the heavens and the earth.’

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Particular Patterns of Behavior
s.d: the system of practices and standards associated with secular society (that is, without reference to any demands or requirements of God)
s.c: αἰών in ⟦1 Corinthians 3:18|1 Corinthians 3:18⟧ may also be rendered as ‘by the way in which people in this world think’ or ‘by the things which people in this world think are right.’ In ⟦Mark 4:19|Mark 4:19⟧ the phrase αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος may be rendered as ‘the cares which people in this world have’ or ‘the way in which people in this world worry about things.’

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: (an idiom, literally: from an age) a point of time preceding another point of time, with a very long interval between (more emphatic than {L:πάλαι<SDBG:πάλαι:000000>}[a], {L:ἔκπαλαι<SDBG:ἔκπαλαι:000000>}[a], {D:67.24})
s.c: Some persons have concluded that ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος must be understood in the sense of ‘from an earlier age,’ but there seems to be no justification for reading a dispensational implication into this idiomatic expression.

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: an exceedingly long period of time from an assumed beginning up to the present
s.g: since all time; from all ages past; from the beginning of time

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: unlimited duration of time, with particular focus upon the future
s.g: always; forever; forever and ever; eternally; (with neg.) never
s.c: See also ⟦Luke 1:33|Luke 1:33⟧; ⟦2 Peter 3:18|2 Peter 3:18⟧; ⟦Jude 1:25|Jude 1:25⟧; ⟦Hebrews 1:8|Hebrews 1:8⟧. The more elaborate expressions employing αἰών are somewhat more emphatic in meaning and are to be found especially in the solemn style of doxologies.

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Powers
s.d: title for supernatural forces and powers: a supernatural power having some particular role in controlling the destiny and activities of human beings
s.g: power; authority; lordship; ruler; wicked force
s.c: Some scholars have believed that it is possible to reconstruct at least in part some of the hierarchy represented by these various supernatural forces and powers, on the basis of the neoplatonic system of nine such powers arranged in three orders of three each. NT terminology and usage does not, however, lend itself to such a classification, and it is difficult, if not impossible, to determine what are the significant differences between these supernatural powers and forces.|For the most part, translators have endeavored to render the various terms in somewhat different ways, for example, ἐξουσία as ‘authority’; δύναμις as ‘power’; κυριότης as ‘ruler’; and phrases such as τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις as ‘wicked spiritual forces in the heavenly world.’ In a number of languages, however, there are simply not enough terms to designate various kinds of powers, authorities, and forces which could be employed in speaking of such supernatural impersonal powers. Accordingly, some translators have simply used a phrase such as ‘any and all kinds of supernatural powers.’ Where it is possible to make certain lexical distinctions between terms and phrases, this, of course, should be done, but in a number of contexts this may be impossible, and accordingly, some explanation in a marginal note may be required if the reader is to understand satisfactorily the intent of the passages in question.

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a title for the Devil, literally: the god of this world) one who has power or authority over this world (or this age) and is so recognized by people of the world
s.g: the god of this world; the Devil
s.c: The expression ‘the god of this world’ may be understood in two senses: (1) the god who rules over this world or (2) the god whom the people of this world trust or worship. Though many persons have traditionally interpreted ‘the god of this world’ as the one who rules over this world, it is the second meaning which probably fits more accurately in the context of ⟦2 Corinthians 4:4|2 Corinthians 4:4⟧.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: (an idiom, literally: sons of this age) persons who hold to the value system of the world
s.g: non-religious people; people of this world; people of this age
s.c: In some instances ‘the people of this world’ may be rendered as ‘the people who live like most people in the world’ or ‘the people who are concerned only about what people say.’ Sometimes the identification with the world is expressed in contrast with people’s attitude concerning God, for example, ‘people who have no use for God.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: (an idiom, literally: yesterday, today, and forever) an unlimited extension of time, from the past into the future
s.g: always; eternally; past and present and future

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to an unlimited duration of time{N:001}
s.c: The most frequent use of αἰώνιος in the NT is with ζωή 'life', for example, ἵνα πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐν αὐτῷ ἔχω ζωὴν αἰώνιον ‘so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life’ ⟦John 3:15|John 3:15⟧. In combination with ζωή there is evidently not only a temporal element, but also a qualitative distinction. In such contexts, αἰώνιος evidently carries certain implications associated with αἰώνιος in relationship to divine and supernatural attributes. If one translates ‘eternal life’ as simply ‘never dying,’ there may be serious misunderstandings, since persons may assume that ‘never dying’ refers only to physical existence rather than to ‘spiritual death.’ Accordingly, some translators have rendered ‘eternal life’ as ‘unending real life,’ so as to introduce a qualitative distinction.

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: an exceedingly long period of time from an assumed beginning up to the present
s.g: since all time; from all ages past; from the beginning of time

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Impurity
s.d: the state of moral impurity, especially in relationship to sexual sin
any substance which is filthy or dirty
pertaining to being ritually unacceptable, either as the result of defilement or because of the very nature of the object itself (for example, ritually unacceptable animals)
s.c: It is possible that there is some subtle distinction in meaning, particularly on a connotative level, between κοινός and ἀκάθαρτος in ⟦Acts 10:14|Acts 10:14⟧, but it is difficult to determine the precise differences of meaning on the basis of existing contexts. The two terms are probably used in ⟦Acts 10:14|Acts 10:14⟧ primarily for the sake of emphasis.

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: to not have a favorable opportunity to do something
s.g: to lack an opportunity; to have no chance to

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: pertaining to the lack of a favorable opportunity for doing something
s.g: unfavorable; when the time is not right

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Goodness
s.d: pertaining to being without fault and hence guileless
s.c: In ⟦Hebrews 7:26|Hebrews 7:26⟧ ἄκακος has a far more positive meaning than merely not being bad. In other words, the negation of κακός bad (LN 88.106) does not produce a term which is merely morally neutral, but it designates something of a clearly positive character.

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Suppose, Think Possible
s.d: pertaining to being unsuspecting or naive with regard to possible deception
s.c: It may be possible to spell out the implications of ἄκακος in ⟦Romans 16:18|Romans 16:18⟧ by translating ‘the minds of people who do not suspect lies.’

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: any kind of plant with sharp projections on its stem and/or branches; regarded as useless; symbol of hardship
s.c: Since plants having thorny projections are almost worldwide in distribution, there is no difficulty in obtaining a satisfactory term for such plants. In some instances, however, a descriptive equivalent may be necessary, for example, ‘plants with piercing points’ or ‘plants that stick into one’s flesh.’

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἄκανθα<SDBG:ἄκανθα:000000>} ‘thorn plant,’ {D:3.17}) pertaining to being made or consisting of thorns; in the NT, only in the phrase ἀκάνθινον στέφανον, a crown made from a plant with sharp projections on its stem and/or branches; symbol of hardship
s.c: It may be necessary to indicate that this crown of thorns is one made of ‘branches of a thorny bush,’ for the crown did not consist merely of thorns but of thorny vines or branches.

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Ripen, Produce Fruit, Bear Seed
s.d: pertaining to not producing seed, fruit, or harvest
s.g: without fruit; bearing no fruit; producing no harvest
s.c: In ⟦Jude 1:12|Jude 1:12⟧ a literal rendering of ‘even in autumn’ might be misleading in some areas in which autumn as a calendrical term might not be the period for bearing fruit. Therefore, it might be better to translate ⟦Jude 1:12|Jude 1:12⟧ as ‘trees that bear no fruit even in the season when they should.’

s.d: pertaining to being useless, in the sense of being unproductive
pertaining to what cannot be criticized
s.c: It may be necessary in some languages to restructure ἀκατάγνωστος and ἀνεπίλημπτος as complete clauses, so that instead of ‘sound words which are above criticism’ in ⟦Titus 2:8|Titus 2:8⟧, one may translate ‘sound words which no one can criticize’ or ‘… against which no one can say anything.’ ‘Above reproach’ in ⟦1 Timothy 6:14|1 Timothy 6:14⟧ may be rendered as ‘in such a way that no one can criticize it.’

s.d: pertaining to not being covered

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judicial Hearing, Inquiry
s.d: pertaining to not having gone through a judicial hearing, with the implication of not having been condemned
pertaining to that which cannot be caused to cease
s.g: cannot be brought to an end; cannot be caused to finish

s.d: pertaining to not ceasing from some activity
to rise up in open defiance of authority, with the presumed intention to overthrow it or to act in complete opposition to its demands
s.g: to rebel against; to revolt; to engage in insurrection; rebellion
s.c: It is possible that ἀκαταστασία in ⟦Luke 21:9|Luke 21:9⟧ denotes merely unsettled conditions, but it is far more likely to carry the meaning of ‘insurrections’ and ‘revolts.’

s.d: violent opposition to someone or something, involving mob action{N:001}
pertaining to being unable to be controlled by something or someone
s.g: not controlled by; not subject to; uncontrolled
s.c: It is also possible to translate ‘it is an evil which cannot be controlled’ as ‘it is an evil which no one can control’ or ‘no one can control this evil.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (an Aramaic term meaning ‘field of blood’) a piece of land, probably south of the valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, which was bought with Judas money

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Holy, Pure
s.d: pertaining to being without a mixture of evil and hence to being pure

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: pertaining to being without change or wavering in one’s faith

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Ripen, Produce Fruit, Bear Seed
s.d: to become or to be ripe
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to ripen’ is ‘to become sweet’ or ‘to become edible.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: extension of time up to and beyond an expected point
the faculty of hearing
s.c: In some languages it may be better to speak about the organs involved rather than the related faculties, for example, ‘if the whole body were an eye, what about the ears?’

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀκούω<SDBG:ἀκούω:000000>}[a] ‘to hear,’ {D:24.52}) that which is heard by someone
s.c: In a number of languages the closest equivalent of ‘message’ would be ‘that which is said’ rather than ‘that which is heard,’ and accordingly, one may perhaps best translate ⟦Romans 10:16|Romans 10:16⟧ as ‘who has believed what we said.’

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀκούω<SDBG:ἀκούω:000002>}[c] ‘to receive news,’ {D:33.212}) the content of the news which is heard
s.c: In a number of languages, however, it is impossible to speak of ‘news spreading.’ It therefore may be necessary to render ⟦Matthew 4:24|Matthew 4:24⟧ as ‘people throughout the whole country of Syria kept hearing from one another about him.’

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to believe something and to respond to it on the basis of having heard
s.g: to accept; to listen to; to listen and respond; to pay attention and respond; to heed

s.d: (a Semitic idiom, literally: to hear with hearing) to listen intently and with presumed continuity
s.g: to listen carefully; to listen and listen

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Desire, Want, Wish
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to itch with respect to hearing) to have one’s ears tickled by what is heard{N:002}
s.g: to have itching ears; to desire to hear what one wants to hear; to be desirous of hearing

s.d: to come/go behind or after someone else
s.g: to follow; to come behind; to go behind

s.d: to follow or accompany someone who takes the lead in determining direction and route of movement
s.g: to accompany as a follower; to follow; to go along with
s.c: ἀκολουθέω differs from ἀκολουθέω (LN 15.144) in that it specifies a factor of accompaniment rather than merely going behind.

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: to be a follower or a disciple of someone, in the sense of adhering to the teachings or instructions of a leader and in promoting the cause of such a leader
s.g: to follow; to be a disciple of
s.c: Though many translators have attempted to employ the metaphorical significance of ‘to follow’ in the sense of ‘to be a disciple of,’ there are certain dangers in a number of languages. For example, ‘to follow’ may often have the connotation of ‘to pursue after with evil intent.’ In many languages the appropriate equivalent of ‘to follow’ (in the sense of ‘to be a disciple’) is literally ‘to accompany’ or ‘to go along with’ or ‘to be in the group of.’

s.d: to have the faculty of hearing in contrast with being deaf{N:002}
s.g: to be able to hear; faculty of hearing

s.d: to receive information about something, normally by word of mouth
s.c: In ⟦Mark 6:29|Mark 6:29⟧ ἀκούω clearly implies more than mere physiological hearing, for the content of the message is included as a significant element in the meaning of ἀκούω. Compare also ἀκοή (LN 33.213).

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to believe something and to respond to it on the basis of having heard
s.g: to accept; to listen to; to listen and respond; to pay attention and respond; to heed

s.d: to listen or pay attention to a person, with resulting conformity to what is advised or commanded{N:004}
s.g: to pay attention to and obey

s.d: to hear and understand a message{N:005}

s.dp: Courts and Legal Procedures › Judicial Hearing, Inquiry
s.d: to give a judicial hearing in a legal matter{N:006}
s.g: to hear a case; to provide a legal hearing; to hear a case in court
s.c: In some languages the most satisfactory way of speaking about ‘a court hearing’ is to describe the relationship between the principal participants. This may sometimes be done by translating ‘for a judge to listen to an accuser and a defender.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to hear into the ear) to hear something in a secret setting
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘what you hear in secret’ may be ‘what you hear when no one else is around’ or ‘what you hear whispered to you.’

s.dp: Understand › Lack of Capacity for Understanding
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to hear heavily with the ears) to be mentally slow or dull in comprehending
s.g: to be slow to understand; to be mentally dull

s.d: (a Semitic idiom, literally: to hear with hearing) to listen intently and with presumed continuity
s.g: to listen carefully; to listen and listen

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Self-Control, Lack of Self-Control
s.d: to fail to exercise self-control
s.g: lack of self-control; failure to control oneself

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Self-Control, Lack of Self-Control
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀκρασία<SDBG:ἀκρασία:000000>} ‘lack of self-control,’ {D:88.91}) pertaining to lacking self-control

s.dp: Features of Objects › Pure, Unadulterated, Undiluted
s.d: pertaining to being pure in the sense of not being diluted and hence at full strength
strict conformity to a norm or standard, involving both detail and completeness
pertaining to strict conformity to a norm or standard, involving both detail and completeness
to acquire information in an exact and accurate manner or to acquire information which is exact and accurate
s.g: to learn exactly; to find out accurately; to ascertain

s.d: pertaining to strict conformity to a norm or standard, involving both detail and completeness
